transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood), Ava Nguyen (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (Starlight Head of Data & ML), Tom Reeves (Starlight Sec Arch), Elena Gomez (Product), Ravi Singh (SRE)

Summary (auto):
- POC scoping focused on data handling: PII, logging/redaction, retention settings, prompt storage for prototyping with Redwood Dedicated vs hosted.
- Agreed success criteria: functional accuracy, throughput (200 rps baseline), 99th perc latency target, no persistent storage of raw PII, and run of benchmark suite.
- Next steps: Redwood to share security docs and benchmark harness; customer to provide anonymized data and success criteria doc; schedule benchmark week of 2026-11-23.

Topics:
- PII handling and redaction
- Logging & observability retention controls
- Prompt & context storage (ephemeral vs persisted)
- Retention policies and configurable TTLs
- Deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC)
- Benchmark sizing and timeline

[00:00:05] Priya Shah: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick off quick — high level objective today is to align on POC scope for data handling concerns, we know starlight is particularly strict around PHI/PII so we want to nail requirements before we run benchmarks.

[00:00:22] Maya Patel: yes thanks priya, our main ask is we need to ensure that nothing that could be PHI is logged or stored unencrypted, and where we need to store prompts for debugging there's a clear redaction flow and TTL.

[00:00:35] Carlos Mendes: understood. quick clarify — is the POC going to use your dev data set or a synthetic/anonymized export?

[00:00:45] Maya Patel: we'll provide an anonymized subset, maybe 10k records to start. tom can comment on what we can share.

[00:00:51] Tom Reeves: yep, security side — we can do an export with direct identifiers removed, still want to know how redact is done if an agent tries to return an identifier in generation. is there on-the-fly redaction or do you recommend client-side masking?

[00:01:05] Liam Chen: good question. Redwood supports a few layers: client-side pre-redaction, runtime filter hooks (we can run regex/PII classifiers at request time), and persistent log redaction before storage. in hosted mode we offer configurable retention windows and an option to disable transcript storage.

[00:01:25] Elena Gomez: does that mean the raw prompt will never be written to disk in hosted mode if we set retention to zero?

[00:01:32] Carlos Mendes: in hosted we have ephemeral in-memory handling for requests, but operational logs/trace can be configured. by default debug logs may include prompt excerpts — but we can disable storing prompts and logs or apply automatic redaction rules. for highest assurance we recommend dedicated or private with customer-managed keys.

[00:01:54] Tom Reeves: customer-managed keys — KMS? hsm? what integrations do you have?

[00:01:58] Priya Shah: we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS and we have HSM options for private deployments. we also support encrypting at rest with your keys and rotating. i'll send the KMS/HSM integration notes.

[00:02:12] Ravi Singh: what about KV cache or prefix caching? if a prompt includes PII are those cached?

[00:02:18] Carlos Mendes: good catch. KV caches are in-memory per-host and not persisted by default; however some configurations support warm cache snapshots for faster warm-up — those snapshots can be disabled. we can explicitly exclude prompt context from caches, or configure cache TTL to be minimal.

[00:02:33] Maya Patel: okay that helps. for the POC success criteria we want: (1) zero persistent storage of raw PHI, (2) ability to redact PII from logs automatically, (3) benchmark demonstrating 99th percentile latency < 350 ms for our typical prompt size, and (4) throughput around 200 rps at x concurrency. is that feasible?

[00:02:54] Carlos Mendes: feasible. couple follow-ups — what's your typical prompt length / tokens?

[00:02:58] Maya Patel: average user prompt is ~45 tokens, full context including patient history is about 750 tokens in some cases.

[00:03:08] Liam Chen: ok that distribution matters. for 750-token contexts we recommend a quantized model variant and we should measure both median and tail latencies. for the POC we'll run two benchmarks: small (<=100 tokens) for user-facing and large (>=500 tokens) for clinician workflows.

[00:03:24] Elena Gomez: timeline — we need results before end of month to decide on a pilot. what's real timeline for a 2-phase POC?

[00:03:30] Priya Shah: typical POC is 3-4 weeks: week 0 - kickoff and security review, week 1 - harness and test dataset, week 2 - run benchmarks & iterate on config (caching, batching), week 3 - present results and remediation. given today is 11/12 we can aim to have benchmark results by 11/30 if datasets are ready.

[00:03:48] Tom Reeves: any SOC2 / ISO docs you can send now for legal?

[00:03:51] Priya Shah: yes, i'll send SOC2 Type II and our security matrix after the call.

[00:03:56] Maya Patel: on logging — we require an audit trail for admin actions but we do not want prompt text to be stored. can you separate administrative audit logs from request payload storage?

[00:04:05] Carlos Mendes: yes, admin audit logs are separated and don't contain full request payloads. for compliance we can provide structured metadata (request id, user id hash, latency, model version) without storing raw prompt content.

[00:04:18] Ravi Singh: how do you handle function/tool calling outputs? sometimes those include extracted entities which could be PHI.

[00:04:25] Liam Chen: function outputs are treated like any generated content; we can apply the same redaction pipeline before persisting. for the POC we can default to no persisting of function outputs unless explicitly allowed.

[00:04:36] Elena Gomez: are there mechanisms to anonymize or pseudonymize candidate outputs for debugging?

[00:04:41] Carlos Mendes: yes, we offer token-level placeholders and entity substitution at post-process. the debug logs can be configured to replace identified PHI with stable pseudonyms to preserve linkability for debugging without exposing raw PHI.

[00:04:55] Tom Reeves: good. one more: retention windows. we need TTL for any stored prompts to be configurable to "0" (no storage) and if stored, automatic deletion after X days. is that available?

[00:05:04] Priya Shah: yes, retention is configurable per-tenant and per-route; you can set storage_disabled, or TTL in days. we'll document the API to change retention and will include in the security matrix.

[00:05:12] Maya Patel: For the benchmarking itself — what metrics will you provide? we want per-route p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost estimate per 1M tokens, and memory footprint.

[00:05:23] Carlos Mendes: benchmark deliverables: p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, tokens per second, effective throughput at target concurrency, and cost per-token estimates using our cost model. we'll provide raw traces (with prompts redacted) and an aggregate report.

[00:05:36] Elena Gomez: speaking of cost model — will you simulate our expected traffic (mix of short and long prompts) to get a realistic ESTIMATE?

[00:05:41] Carlos Mendes: yes we'll run a mixed workload that mirrors your distribution. please provide sample distribution percentages for short/med/long.

[00:05:48] Maya Patel: short 60%, medium 30%, long 10%.

[00:05:51] Priya Shah: perfect. we'll size benchmark: target sustained throughput 200 rps with bursts to 400 for 30s. for resource sizing we'll propose a Dedicated pool spec (gpu count, memory) and also show hosted numbers to compare cost and tail latency.

[00:06:06] Ravi Singh: for network isolation — if we go private VPC, can we still run your rollout and tracing tooling? we need the control plane separated but still want some observability.

[00:06:14] Priya Shah: yes, Private supports a customer-managed control plane where telemetry can be sent to your monitoring stack; we also support a hybrid where traces are forwarded to your endpoint via secure connector, and you can opt out of sending full prompts.

[00:06:27] Tom Reeves: what about egress — do logs leave region, and can you guarantee data residency?

[00:06:31] Carlos Mendes: we can pin deployment to region and we won't replicate logs outside region for Private/Dedicated. Hosted by default follows region tenancy but for strict residency we recommend Private.

[00:06:42] Elena Gomez: any risk of model probing exposing sensitive info from training data?

[00:06:46] Liam Chen: we only use open / vetted models and we recommend using curated model variants; model extraction risk is primarily a training data issue. for POCs we can run guardrails and output filters to catch hallucinated sensitive strings.

[00:06:58] Maya Patel: ok to confirm acceptance criteria we will sign off the POC if:
- 1) Benchmarks meet 99th perc latency < 350 ms on short prompts and acceptable tails for long prompts with config tuned.
- 2) No persistent storage of raw PHI unless explicitly consented; retention TTLs enforced.
- 3) Redaction/pseudonymization available for debug traces.
- 4) Clear cost per-token estimate and resource sizing for pilot.

[00:07:20] Priya Shah: sounds good. to be concrete: i'll send SOC2, KMS/HSM notes, and our security matrix; carlos will send the benchmark harness and sample scripts for a 50k token run and mixed distribution. maya will provide anonymized dataset by 11/19. we aim to run benchmarks week of 11/23 and demo results 11/30.

[00:07:37] Elena Gomez: will you include an option to run the same harness against dedicated capacity os private env? we want apples-to-apples latency and cost comparisons.

[00:07:44] Carlos Mendes: yes we'll spin up both hosted and a dedicated sandbox — or instrument a private dev node if you prefer — and run identical traffic. note dedicated will likely have lower tail latency for heavy context sizes.

[00:07:56] Tom Reeves: can we get an architecture note describing where redaction happens in the pipeline?

[00:08:00] Priya Shah: yes, i'll include a short architecture diagram in the security package.

[00:08:04] Maya Patel: last question — if we find edge cases where redaction misses something, what's the remediation SLA?

[00:08:09] Ava Nguyen: remediation depends on severity; for POC we commit to triage within 24 hours and patch redaction patterns within a few days; for enterprise contract we'll add specific SLAs.

[00:08:20] Priya Shah: great — any other items?

[00:08:23] (brief silence)

[00:08:26] Maya Patel: nothing else, thanks everyone.

[00:08:29] Priya Shah: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and the benchmark plan.

Recap / Next steps (auto):
- Priya to send SOC2, security matrix, KMS/HSM integration notes and retention API documentation (due 2026-11-13).
- Carlos to provide benchmark harness + mixed workload scripts and initial sizing recommendation (due 2026-11-16).
- Maya to provide anonymized dataset and success criteria doc (due 2026-11-19).
- Run benchmarks week of 2026-11-23, present findings 2026-11-30.

References / Shared artifacts:
